rationale:
ROUND 3 of migration 516. Round 2 = REVISE, gated by prior_art_librarian on two HIGH objections, both of which were right, and both are now settled by measurement rather than by argument.

(A) GATING #1 — 'the landmine edit is NOT in this submission's edit list, and the snapshot still shows the generic text, not the version-qualified heading claimed.' BOTH HALVES CORRECT, and the second half found a defect in my fix that I would not have seen. I had appended the version qualifier to the END of the heading, so a reader that truncates sees only the opening clause — which is the ORIGINAL failure (readers match on the heading) RELOCATED, not removed. The heading now LEADS with the state: '`?` in a step's action `config`: INERT up to chassis v1.0.1320, LIVE from v1.0.1321 (2026-08-20) — ...'. Verified at the surface seats actually read, not just in the file: all four doc_notes rows for that entry now carry the new body. And the landmine file is now IN the edit list below, which it should have been.

(B) GATING #2 — 'marker is live on v1.0.1321 is a deployed-binary liveness fact ... must be settled by a pod-grep, not a DB or code-index tier.' AGREED, and done: kubectl exec <chassis pod> -- grep -aqF '0483e7f4e410168d30ed2d86dcbb820d8c28a383' /proc/1/exe returns PRESENT, with a fake-sha absent-control returning exit 1. Combined with `git merge-base --is-ancestor ecc419bd1 0483e7f4e` (true; a later commit as control, false) that settles it AT THE ARTEFACT. Why the usual capability probe was unavailable and this route was needed: ecc419bd1 adds NO new string literal (its quotable phrases are in comments, which Go strips) and no new exported symbol — all closures and locals — so there is nothing in the binary to probe FOR except the build stamp itself.

STRONGER STILL, and new since round 2: the marker now has a LIVE PRODUCTION WIRE. Migration 515 (another session's, page-build-handler/plan_sections `page_type?`) was APPLIED at 2026-08-21 13:19:19Z — verified in agent_definitions, which also answers the round-2 medium objection that 515's landing was unverified. Since it landed: page-build-handler/`page_type` conflict rows = 0 against 4 pbh runs (last row 2026-08-20 15:11:38Z, before the wire). DETECTION FLOOR STATED: 4 runs is a thin sample — under the pre-wire behaviour the class fired on roughly the 13/31 of runs where the page's own record is present to conflict with the siblings, so P(0 rows over 4 runs) is around 10%. That is CONSISTENT with the marker working in production and is NOT proof of it; I am not claiming more.

(C) debug_historian, medium — RIGHT and fixed: after a successful apply the discovery walk necessarily finds zero unmarked carriers (the keys were renamed), so 'refuse on zero' made an idempotent re-run indistinguishable from a broken walk. The zero now branches on the MARKED population: >0 marked raises 'ALREADY APPLIED ... not a failure'; 0 and 0 raises the walk-is-broken error. Proven by INDUCING the state — pre-applying the rename in the same transaction and then running the migration — not by reading the code.

(D) guardian, medium (the acks file couples 515's entry to 516's gate): the coupling is visible but it CANNOT perturb, and that is a property of the code rather than a promise. The gate resolves acknowledgement per (action, field) key — `acked[step.Action+"."+base]` — so a correction to `plan_sections.page_type` cannot change the acknowledged state of `create_tool_component.related_pages` or `deploy_tool_to_site.related_pages`. Keeping the entry is what stops the gate being RED ON ARRIVAL for the next person who runs it, which it would otherwise be, for a reason unrelated to them. Live proof: run against today's fleet reports 1 wire, 0 unacknowledged, exit 0.

(E) guardian, low (a third carrier running a known action would be converted without its own absence read): absence-safety is a property of the CONSUMING ACTION, not of the step that wires it — which is exactly why the acks are keyed on the action. Any carrier running create_tool_component or deploy_tool_to_site reaches the same relatedPagesFromInputs helper and the same instrumented `no_related_pages` skip that was read first-hand. A carrier running anything else ABORTS the migration.

(F) tooling_provenance, medium (the acks-ledger pattern is machine-regenerated; hand-writing may be counted as ZERO): the cited landmine is about optional_key_budget_acks.json, whose risk is that check.py carries a MIRRORED LITERAL that drifts from the file — which is why that pair has a parity test. optional_explicit_wire_acks.json has no mirror and no cron literal: it is read from disk at run time by the audit itself, so there is nothing to regenerate and nothing to drift. The disanalogy is the answer; if the council would rather it were generated, say so and I will not hand-author the next entry.

(G) editquality, low (the abort-on-unknown-action guard is not in the sketch): now shown verbatim in the sketch below.

Unchanged from round 2: the file is still HELD behind migration 512's demand control (tool-generator runs since its boundary: still 0), and the absence-safety read stands.

edits.rationale: Discovery-driven, not a hand-typed list (round-1 editquality + the validation.WalkSteps landmine). One recursive walk with NO path literals finds every step config carrying an unmarked related_pages at any depth, under either loop-container spelling; ABORTS on a carrier running an action whose absence-handling was not read; refuses to succeed on zero found. VERIFY asserts the global postcondition (no unmarked carrier anywhere, every marked one on the intended path) rather than re-checking the paths just edited.
edits.sketch: FOR tgt IN (WITH RECURSIVE walk ... WHERE path[last]='config' AND node ? 'related_pages') LOOP IF tgt.step_action NOT IN ('create_tool_component','deploy_tool_to_site') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '516: % step % runs %, which is NOT one of the two actions whose absence-handling was read ...'; END IF; jsonb_set(default_config, tgt.config_path||ARRAY['related_pages?'], ...) then #- the unmarked key. END LOOP; IF found=0 THEN (count marked) -> 'ALREADY APPLIED' if >0 else walk-is-broken. Dry run: 2 converted, global VERIFY clean, ROLLBACK; already-applied branch proven by inducing the post-apply state.

plan.risks: Applying this before 512 is verified would silence both tool-generator classes at once and make 512 permanently unverifiable - which is why the file is _HOLD with that as its stated condition, and the whole reason it is not simply applied today. The second step (tool-deployer) has no logged rows, so its conversion is prophylactic: if some caller of deploy_tool_to_site were relying on the searched value, this removes it silently - I judge that unlikely to the point of being the desired outcome (the searched value is another tool's pages by construction), but it is the one behaviour change here with no instrument behind it. After apply, 330's verification needs fresh tool-generator demand (~16 runs/24h historically, but 0 in the last 18 h) and its instrument-alive control must come from another agent's class. This does not close 330's general half - an unmarked wired-but-empty field anywhere else still falls through - which stays candidate 2, gated on the 269-pair unsampled remainder. ROUND 2 addition: the discovery walk now decides WHICH configs get edited, so its abort-on-unknown-action guard is what bounds it - a carrier running an unread action stops the migration rather than being converted. That is deliberately stricter than the hand-typed version it replaces, which would simply have ignored such a carrier.
